ingredients.item: Long sweet green peppers (sivri, Cubanelle or Anaheim)

instructions: Cut the stems off the peppers, split them open, and scrape out the seeds. Slice them into thin strips, about 1/4 inch wide.
In a bowl, beat the eggs with 3/4 tsp of the salt, the pepper and the thyme.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the peppers and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft and a few edges turn golden.
Turn the heat to medium-low and pour the eggs over the peppers. Stir slowly with a spatula, pulling the set egg in from the edges, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat when no runny egg is left but the eggs still look glossy. They keep cooking in the pan.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve right away, straight from the pan.
method_notes: Nefis Yemek Tarifleri (the lead, 5.0 from 5 votes) cooks sliced peppers in fat until soft, then stirs beaten eggs through until set; Yemek.com's version is the same with thyme and salt in the eggs. The sources use butter or butter with oil; this one uses olive oil only so it stays dairy-free, and it skips the optional kashar cheese for the same reason. Pepper amounts differ a lot between sources, so this scales to the 8 eggs with 6 long sweet peppers.
